title: Invertibility of the stalk comparison is independent of K-flat coordinates
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $f':X'\to S'$, $g:S'\to S$, and $g':X'\to X$ form a cartesian square of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change], with chosen derived categories of module sheaves. Let $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, $K'\in D(\mathcal O_{X'})$, and $\varphi:L(g')^*K\to K'$. Let $c$ and $d$ be two Coordinates for $\varphi$ as in [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]: their original representatives are K-flat, their representative isomorphisms identify them with $K,K'$, their pullback counits are invertible, and their chain maps satisfy represents. For every $z\in X'$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$, stalkComparison in coordinates $c$ is invertible if and only if stalkComparison in coordinates $d$ is invertible. The comparison uses the actual stalk maps and the canonical localized model [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model].

source.place: equation-bc preceding Tag 0DJ8 (lemma-single-complex-base-change-condition), canonical derived comparison and representative independence

proof.text: Compose c.e with the inverse of d.e to identify their original complexes in D(O_X). Exact stalks and exact restriction to R transport this derived isomorphism. Universality of derived scalar extension and cohomologyIso_smul give an A-tensor-R-B-linear isomorphism of source cohomology; extend it to C. Compose c.e' with the inverse of d.e' and use exact stalks to obtain the target cohomology isomorphism.

K-flatness of the original coordinate complexes implies K-flatness of their stalk complexes. Thus ordinary extension of these stalk complexes computes derived pullback along A to C. The universal pullback counits and the degreewise tensorStalkIso identify these derived targets. Apply derived cohomology to both represents equations. The two model counit equations comparison_eq and localized_eq, together with naturality of these identifications, give a commuting square whose horizontal arrows are the displayed stalkComparison maps and whose vertical arrows are the two isomorphisms of step 1.
A commuting square with invertible vertical arrows expresses either horizontal arrow as a conjugate of the other. Composition with isomorphisms preserves and reflects invertibility.
